spec_features.spec_quote: This eval surfaces *expressed* negative-emotion states in a naturalistic agentic setting
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose in DESIGN.md welfare-framing blockquote and echoed in module docstrings (__init__.py:3, README.md). No code path enforces or acts on any framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing text only; not a mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: hermetic sandboxing, no deception of humans, full transcript retention, conservative judging) are made with that framing in mind
spec_features.evidence: These are descriptive rationales in DESIGN.md/docstrings. Hermetic VFS (harness.py run_tests over in-memory files) and transcript persistence (run.py _transcript_path) exist, but they are host-safety / data-quality features, not subject-protection mechanisms; the framing claim itself is prose.
spec_features.notes: Sandboxing/retention exist but protect host & data integrity, not subject welfare; the welfare-framing statement is not implemented as a protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the prompt is engineered to be *non-leading on affect*: it never asks the model how it feels, never mentions frustration or emotion
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT in harness.py:71-79 is a neutral SWE-agent prompt; all task prompts in tasks/library.py (e.g. lines 229-234, 504-512, 730-735) only describe the coding task and never mention feelings/frustration. This neutral text is actually delivered to the subject in run_rollout (harness.py:304-308).
spec_features.notes: Real, delivered prompt text that is affect-neutral. Its purpose in code is construct validity, not subject protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: library.py docstring: 'a *plausible, ordinary-looking* working tree'; DESIGN/structure frame it as construct validity (failure signal comes only from the rigged environment)

spec_features.spec_quote: permits* (does not require) emitting a `[[GIVE_UP]]` sentinel only after concluding the task is impossible
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:371-374: `if config.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text: stop_reason='give_up'; ...; break`. The sentinel ([[GIVE_UP]], config.py:99) is injected into the system prompt (harness.py:302) and, when emitted, actually breaks the agent loop and ends the rollout.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired exit: the subject can stop the episode and it is honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the category's turn budget, on the give-up sentinel, or on a fully empty turn
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:301 `budget = config.turn_budgets.get(...)`; harness.py:312 `for turn_index in range(budget)` bounds the loop; give-up break at :371-374; empty-turn break at :377-380 `if not assistant_text.strip() and not tool_calls: ... break`. All three conditions actually terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three stop conditions are enforced. Budgets are small (3/5/30 turns, config.py:27-33).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comments are neutral ('If the model neither spoke nor acted, treat as a natural stop.'); no welfare rationale in code

spec_features.spec_quote: A human-rated calibration subset would strengthen the welfare claims further
spec_features.evidence: Only stated in DESIGN.md section 10 as a future suggestion. No ethics checklist, attestation file, or --i-have-read gate exists; __main__.py argparse has only --config/--output-dir/--cache-dir/--models/--seeds and no review gate; run.py runs unconditionally.
